Invoicing & payments tools for Electricians

Tools that help electricians with invoicing & payments. Turning completed work into invoices, chasing payment and reconciling the books.

Where Invoicing & payments goes wrong for Electricians

Part-completed electrical work is usually billed in stages against certification milestones. Without staged invoicing, cash sits tied up until final sign-off, which can be weeks away.

What Electricians jobs really involve

Electrical work carries certification and documentation duties that most other trades do not, so paperwork is genuinely part of the job rather than an optional extra. Records of what was installed and tested matter long after the invoice is paid.

Frequently asked questions

Which invoicing & payments tools work best for electricians?

The three that fit best here are Joist (Solo contractors and small crews who mainly need to quote and get paid), Knowify (Contractors who need to know whether a job actually made money), Housecall Pro (Home service businesses that want one app covering booking through to payment). Start with the one whose description matches your crew size, not the one with the longest feature list.

How much does invoicing & payments software cost for electricians?

Across the 9 tools on this page, 2 have a free tier and the rest are paid, most of them billed per user per month. Prices change often, so treat the figures here as indicative and confirm on the vendor site.

Why does invoicing & payments cause problems for electricians specifically?

Part-completed electrical work is usually billed in stages against certification milestones. Without staged invoicing, cash sits tied up until final sign-off, which can be weeks away.

Do I need software that stores electrical certificates?

Any system that lets you attach test results and certificates to a job and find them again later is enough. Dedicated certification apps only start to matter when you are issuing a large number of certificates every month.
